Repression occurs when a repressor protein binds to the operator region, blocking RNA polymerase from accessing the promoter and thus preventing transcription. Attenuation is a more complex mechanism where the structure of the transcribed RNA itself can influence whether the full operon is transcribed; this often involves the formation of specific secondary structures in the RNA that can either terminate transcription prematurely or allow it to proceed, depending on the presence or absence of certain molecules. These mechanisms work together to ensure precise regulation of gene expression in response to environmental conditions.
